verdicts.reason: All six quotes exist verbatim, but both halves of the claimed invention are answered by the files the evidence itself cites. (a) CITES is definitively NOT a listing-publish blocker: 13.07.03-cites-export-compliance.md:23 — 'Determination gates bid (13.05.02 D-01) and checkout (13.06.01 D-02)'; :31 — 'Buyer proceeds knowingly, or the listing shows as domestic-only for them' (i.e. it publishes); D-05 at :83 — 'Determination is recomputed live at each commitment gate, never served from a listing-time snapshot'; DT-03 at :62 explicitly rejects listing-time computation. DT-02 at :61 frames CITES as overriding 'the domain-wide never stall the flow instinct for cross-border only' — the domain index D-03 rollup is summarising the never-stall PRINCIPLE, and its own citation resolves the scope. No reading of 13.07.03 puts CITES on the publish gate, so Implementer A's and C's divergence is not available. (b) Payout onboarding: the file that explicitly owns the publish transaction states the count and the category. 13.03.01:25 — 'This file owns media and the demo, the draft/publish transaction'; :27 and the table at :31-32 enumerate exactly two; D-03 at :222 scopes it as 'the only hard publish prerequisite' surfaced 'at draft start, not at publish' — a prerequisite, distinct from 13.02.02 D-03's degradation-gate rule; and 13.12:126 independently corroborates 'no payout method is the flow's second and only other publish blocker'. 13.02.02 D-03's 'only publish-blocking rule' is a locally-scoped claim inside a disclosure file, resolved by the owning node plus a corroborating sibling.

Both quotes verbatim (13.03-listings-inventory-index.md:44; gear-marketplace-index.md:115). The stated forced invention — 'whether CITES is or is not an exception to the never-stall rule at the listing layer' — is answered flatly and repeatedly in the cross-referenced unit: 13.07.03-cites-export-compliance.md:23 gates bid and checkout only, :31 has the listing publishing as domestic-only, and D-05 at :83 forbids any listing-time snapshot ('never served from a listing-time snapshot'), with DT-03 at :62 rejecting listing-time computation by name. So 13.03 D-01's 'single exception' is correct AT THE LISTING LAYER, and the failure scenario (a CITES-restricted instrument publishing with no export gate in the listing path) is not a defect but the prescribed behaviour — the gate lives at 13.05.02 D-01 and 13.06.01 D-02. The domain index's rollup phrasing is imprecise about which flow CITES stalls, but the citation it carries removes the ambiguity, and no publish-gate implementer is left inventing.

Confirmed against the file (bold emphasis in the auditor's quotes is theirs; the substance is verbatim). 13.02.01-condition-grading-scale.md:39 Requires cell reads 'Cosmetic flaws <= light; at most one professionally-executed, stable, disclosed structural repair'; :55 'The cross-check is a pure function of the disclosed flaw set (13.02.02) -> a ceiling'; :63 'structural | repaired (professional, stable) | Ceiling: Excellent'; :71 'The lowest applicable ceiling wins.' The specified carrier is provably count-blind: D-14 at :192 fixes the projection as 'an authored (axis, severity-token) pair on each severity option' — per-option, with no cardinality term — and D-15 at :193 restates the split as 'professionally-executed and stable caps at Excellent' with no count. Sub-domain D-04 (13.02-condition-originality-disclosure-index.md:41) and the CX trigger chain (13.02-...-cx.md:32) both restate it singularly. E-27 at :118 walks the professional-repair case and never mentions a second repair. Not tracked: Q-01..Q-06 at :199-204 cover the cosmetic descriptor, label choice, non-visual evidence, grade distribution, unmatched comps and off-platform corroboration — none the repair count. Crucially, D-14's own rationale ('Authoring the ceiling grade directly on the option was rejected (it rewrites six Requires cells)') shows the Requires cells are treated as normative and load-bearing, so 'at most one' is not decorative prose — yet the ratified machinery cannot compute it. Two disclosed professional structural repairs therefore yield Excellent under the ceiling machinery and non-Excellent under the Requires cell, with nothing adjudicating. Downgraded from the auditor's own framing only in that their scenario mis-derives the alternative grade (Very Good satisfies its Requires cell, not Good) — the Excellent/not-Excellent divergence is real. Warning, not blocking: the domain is still constructible, one cell is unenforceable.

Both quotes verbatim (13.02.01:105; 13.03.02:245), but the two statements compose without contradiction and the finding's supporting premise is false. E-14 is not a platform mandate to cancel — its seller-facing copy reads 'You can't lower the condition on a live auction with bids. Cancel the auction to regrade', i.e. cancellation is the seller's route TO a regrade, not an obligation triggered by the attempt. D-10 makes that route unavailable inside 12h (13.03.02:141 edge row: 'Blocked (D-10)'). Both refusals hold simultaneously: no downward edit, no seller end. The post-close path is then fully specified, not invented — 13.02.01 E-15 at :106, 'Post-purchase, pre-dispatch downward regrade... Seller may record the correction; buyer gets an immediate notification and a one-click cancel with full refund', reinforced by 13.03.02 D-08 at :243 and D-09 at :244 (72h auto-void favouring the buyer). The finding's claim that '13.05.02 specifies no cancellation path' is wrong — 13.05.02-auctions-bidding.md:44 carries 'Seller cancels mid-auction | Bidders have relied on it; cancellation is not free | Cancellation reason + CX-M08 consequence'. And the premise underlying D-10's window is itself tracked: 13.03.02:261 Q-03 '[OWNER] Does a bid bind the seller, or only the bidder? D-10's 12h no-end window assumes it binds both... must be answered jointly with 13.05.02' | User | /create-prd, mirrored in the dependency note at :213.

Both quotes are verbatim (gear-marketplace-index.md:54; 13.11-local-pickup-meetup-safety.md:5), but the finding's distinguishing premise — 'All 49 other index/child status pairs in the domain match; this is the sole divergence' — is demonstrably false. A programmatic pass over all 65 files and every index Children row in the domain returns three mismatches, all in the same table: gear-marketplace-index.md:52 -> 13.09-tradein-consignment-index.md (index [BREADTH] vs own [SURFACE]), :53 -> 13.10-gear-rental-backline-index.md (index [BREADTH] vs own [SURFACE]), and :54 -> 13.11 (index [SURFACE] vs own [PARTIAL]). That is uniform staleness in one dated rollup column, not a targeted contradiction: the table sits under 'Breadth Pass Summary (2026-07-16)' while 13.11 advanced afterwards (its Q-01 at :90 is marked resolved '/ideate-validate, 2026-07-21'). The node file is self-authoritative on its own depth and carries the complete tracking the failure scenario worries about — 13.11 Q-02 (User, /create-prd-security), Q-03 (Agent, /create-prd-security), Q-04 (Agent, /write-be-spec with domain 15), Q-05 (Agent, /write-be-spec) at :91-94, plus D-04/P-09 at :84. No product behaviour is invented, and the state the finding fears (a node re-worked or treated as unsettled) is contradicted by the node's own routed, owned, stage-targeted questions.
